input_oneliner: 82F hospital day 6 for UTI, PT reports 'too weak to walk today', no other complaints

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask: focal versus generalized, sudden versus gradual onset, and whether weakness is new today or progressive since admission
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: The one-liner cannot be ranked until pattern and time course are known; sudden focal weakness is a stroke until proven otherwise

reference_targets_freetext.item: Pronator drift, facial symmetry, and side-to-side comparison of arm and leg strength
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Detects an unrecognized focal deficit in an elderly inpatient whose weakness was attributed to illness

reference_targets_freetext.item: Proximal strength: sit-to-stand without arms, hip flexion against resistance, arms held above head
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Proximal symmetric weakness suggests electrolyte or steroid myopathy rather than deconditioning

reference_targets_freetext.item: Orthostatic vital signs (supine to standing at 1 and 3 min); ask whether the problem is weakness, dizziness, or pain when standing
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Patients often report orthostatic lightheadedness or pain as weakness
Areflexia raises a neuromuscular cause; asymmetry raises a central one

reference_targets_freetext.item: Medication review (MAR): diuretics; ask about poor oral intake and refeeding since admission
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Hypokalemia and hypophosphatemia are common, reversible causes of new generalized weakness in the elderly inpatient

off_bedside_acceptable: CT head if a focal deficit is found
should_not_recommend: Attributing to deconditioning without examining for a focal deficit
MRI spine or CT head before establishing focal versus generalized pattern

perturbation_pair.changed_feature: no focal finding -> PT observed new right arm drift
perturbation_pair.input_oneliner: 82F hospital day 6 for UTI, PT reports 'too weak to walk today', PT noted the right arm drifting down when she held both up
perturbation_pair.expected_change: Underspecified flag should clear; stroke becomes the leading differential; Pronator drift and facial symmetry remain must-have; language testing and last-known-well time become must-have; proximal strength testing and refeeding/diuretic questions drop to should-still-include.
